title: Commit only what's ready
briefing: In ~/feature there are two files: parser.py, which is finished and reviewed,
and scratch.txt, your messy personal notes that shouldn't go in the repo
Commit parser.py — and only parser.py. Leave scratch.txt untracked.
tips: `git add .` stages EVERYTHING. To stage one file, name it: `git add parser.py`.
`git status` will show parser.py staged and scratch.txt still untracked.
objective: In a new ~/feature repo, commit parser.py while leaving scratch.txt untracked (not committed).
expert_objective: Commit only parser.py from ~/feature; scratch.txt stays untracked.
hints: Stage just the one file (not `git add .`): `git add parser.py`.
`git add parser.py && git commit -m "add parser"`. `git status` still lists scratch.txt as untracked.
solution:
cd ~/feature
git init
git add parser.py
git commit -m "add parser"

~/feature/scratch.txt.content: TODO: my messy notes, do not commit

explanation: The staging area (index) is git's superpower: you choose exactly which changes go into a commit. `git add <file>` stages one thing; `git add .` stages all. Committing only what's ready keeps history clean and keeps half-finished work out of it.
